title: To fulfill all righteousness (Matthew 3:13–17)
hook: John protests; Jesus insists on being baptized like everyone else
tomorrow: how do you answer a voice that quotes the Bible back?

segments.voice: Yesterday John asked for a turning you can see. Your line was bear fruit. Today the line at his river gets one more person.

Shoes off, belt off, everyone shuffling forward at airport security, the executive and the college kid holding the same gray bin. A line makes everyone the same height. There's a line at the Jordan too: people waiting their turn to go under with John, confessing their sins. And Matthew says: "Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him." Not to watch. To get in line.
screen: `THE SAME GRAY BIN.` → `A LINE AT THE RIVER.` → `JESUS GETS IN IT.`

segments.voice: John sees who it is and tries to stop him: "I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?" Fair question. Why would the mightier one ask for a washing meant for people confessing their sins? Jesus answers: "Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness." Suffer means let. Righteousness here is doing what's right in God's eyes, all of it, nothing skipped. "Then he suffered him." So feel the scene: the same muddy bank, the same cold river, the same wet hair as the person ahead of him. Matthew doesn't say more about why, and Christians read it more than one way. Some hear him standing with sinners, shoulder to shoulder with the whole human crowd. Some hear an example for everyone baptized after him. Some hear plain obedience. Then, coming up out of the water, he sees "the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him," and a voice says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." One to tell a friend tonight: in Matthew the voice comes before Jesus has preached a sermon or healed anyone. What he has done is stand in line.
screen: `JOHN: COMEST THOU TO ME?` · `SUFFER IT TO BE SO NOW.` · `THE SAME COLD RIVER.` · `THIS IS MY BELOVED SON.` · then, large: `IN LINE WITH SINNERS.`

segments.voice: Stand up, if you can, feet planted and hands loose at your sides, the way people stand in a line. Let the strangers you'll wait beside this week come to mind, at a register, a bus stop, a clinic, and stay right there with them: not ahead, not apart, one more person waiting.
To fulfill all righteousness. Jesus' answer to John: let it be so, in the same river as everyone else.
Pocket this one: in line with sinners, which is where the voice from heaven found him. Go well.

original.note: Greek: righteousness, also justice. the word behind righteousness in Matthew 3:15.

trapdoor: what you thought: Jesus' baptism was a private ceremony, just for him.
what it means: Jesus joins the same washing as the crowd, over John's protest, to fulfil all righteousness.
what a scholar hears: Matthew gives no reason beyond righteousness. Christians read it as solidarity, as example, or as obedience, and the voice from heaven comes before any sermon or healing.
guess: doing all God asks, even waiting in line

recall: a change that shows in what you do
a family line, traced name by name

chat.meaning: Jesus went down into the same water as the people confessing their sins, and the voice from heaven found him in that line.

Galilee.meaning: the region Jesus came from to the Jordan
